question: Under the FMCSA Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) regulations effective February 7, 2022, who must complete ELDT before taking required tests?
choice_a: New CDL applicants seeking a Class A or B for the first time, and current holders upgrading from Class B to Class A or adding a P, S, or H endorsement for the first time
choice_b: Only drivers seeking a hazardous materials endorsement
choice_c: All CDL holders renewing an existing license
explanation: The manual states ELDT affects new CMV drivers obtaining a Class A or B for the first time, current holders upgrading from Class B to Class A, and those adding an S, P, or H endorsement for the first time.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, FMCSA Rule 49 CFR 380 Special Training Requirements

question: Who is exempt from the ELDT training requirement according to the manual?
choice_c: Drivers who previously held an out-of-state CDL or a lapsed CDL, and CLP holders from before February 7, 2022 who convert before their CLP expires
explanation: The manual lists exceptions for drivers with a prior out-of-state or lapsed CDL, and for returning drivers who held a CLP prior to February 7, 2022, as long as they convert to a full CDL before the CLP expires.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, FMCSA Rule 49 CFR 380 Special Training Requirements

question: Under the Maryland CDL manual, a combination of vehicles is defined as a commercial motor vehicle (CMV) if it has a Gross Combination Weight Rating (GCWR) of at least what weight?
explanation: The manual defines a CMV as including any combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Commercial Motor Vehicle

question: A vehicle is classified as a CMV regardless of weight if it is designed to transport how many passengers, including the driver?
explanation: The manual states a CMV includes any vehicle designed to transport 16 or more passengers, including the driver.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Commercial Motor Vehicle

question: A Maryland Class A CDL authorizes operation of a combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the towed vehicle's GVWR exceeds what weight?
explanation: Class A authorizes tractor/trailer or combination vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 or more pounds if the GVWR of the towed vehicle is in excess of 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Maryland Commercial Driver License Classes

question: A Class B CDL authorizes operation of a single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, towing a vehicle not exceeding what GVWR?
explanation: Class B authorizes any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 or more pounds, and towing a vehicle not in excess of 10,000 pounds GVWR.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Maryland Commercial Driver License Classes

question: A Class C license covers single vehicles under 26,001 lbs GVWR that are included in the CDL program because they transport 16 or more passengers, or because they:
choice_d: Are used exclusively for farm work
explanation: Class C vehicles under 26,001 lbs GVWR fall under the CDL program if designed to transport 16+ passengers or used to transport hazardous materials requiring placarding.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Maryland Commercial Driver License Classes

question: Which CDL endorsement is required to pull double or triple trailers, even though triple trailers are not permitted on Maryland roads?
explanation: The T endorsement (Double/Triple Trailers) must be added to a CDL to pull double or triple trailers, though the manual notes triple trailers are not permitted on Maryland roads.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.2.2 CDL Endorsements & Restrictions, T - Double and Triple Trailers

question: An N (tank vehicle) endorsement is required for any tank that holds more than how many gallons, when the total capacity of all tanks is 1,000 gallons or more?
explanation: The N endorsement applies to any tank holding more than 119 gallons where the total capacity of all tanks is 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.2.2 CDL Endorsements & Restrictions, N - Tank Vehicle

question: The X endorsement shows that a driver has passed the special knowledge tests for which two categories?
explanation: The X endorsement combines tank vehicle and hazardous materials, required for tank vehicles hauling hazardous materials or waste requiring placards.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.2.2 CDL Endorsements & Restrictions, X - Combination Hazardous Materials and Tank Vehicle

question: Which endorsements may be added to a Commercial Learner's Permit (CLP)?
explanation: The manual states that only P (Passenger), S (School Bus), and N (Tank Vehicle) endorsements may be added to a CLP.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.2.2 CDL Endorsements & Restrictions

question: A farm vehicle is excluded from CDL requirements if it is operated within how many miles of the farmer's farm and not used for common or contract carrier operations?
explanation: The manual excludes farm vehicles used to transport agricultural products, machinery, or supplies within 150 miles of the person's farm, when not used for common or contract carrier operations.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.2.1 CDL Classifications, Vehicles Excluded From CDL Requirement

question: Before driving a CMV, a driver must obtain what document from a Medical Examiner listed in the National Registry of Certified Medical Examiners?
explanation: A person may not drive a CMV unless physically qualified, which requires a Medical Examiner's Certificate through a Medical Examiner within the National Registry of Certified Medical Examiners.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Physical Qualifications (49 CFR 391.41)

question: The MVA will NOT consider an intrastate medical waiver for a driver who holds which endorsement(s)?
choice_a: Hazardous Materials, Passenger, or School Bus
explanation: The manual states the MVA will not consider an intrastate waiver for an individual who maintains a Hazardous Materials, Passenger, and/or School Bus endorsement.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Physical Qualifications (49 CFR 391.41)

question: Which self-certification category applies to a driver qualified to drive a CMV across state lines under Title 49 CFR Part 391 without needing an MVA medical waiver?
explanation: Non-Excepted Interstate (NI) means the CDL holder is qualified to drive a CMV across state lines in accordance with Title 49 CFR Part 391 of the FMCSR.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Self-Certification

question: A "Non-Excepted Intrastate (NA)" self-certification means the driver:
choice_a: Is qualified to drive a commercial vehicle ONLY within Maryland and has an approved MVA CDL Medical Waiver
choice_b: Drives across state lines for excepted activities only
choice_c: Must renew their CDL every year
choice_d: Is exempt from all federal medical requirements
explanation: Non-Excepted Intrastate (NA) means the CDL holder is qualified to drive ONLY within Maryland and has an approved MVA CDL Medical Waiver.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Self-Certification

question: A CDL holder with an S (school bus) endorsement must obtain a new Medical Examiner's Certificate how often?
explanation: As a CDL driver holding an S endorsement, the driver must obtain a new Medical Examiner's Certificate annually, or the S endorsement is automatically removed.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, School Bus Endorsement

question: What is the minimum age to drive a commercial motor vehicle across state lines (interstate)?
explanation: The manual states you must be 21 years of age to drive a CMV across state lines (interstate).
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Commercial Drivers License Learners Instructional Permit

question: What is the minimum age to drive a CMV within Maryland only (intrastate)?
explanation: The manual states you must be 18 years of age to drive a CMV within Maryland (intrastate).
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Commercial Drivers License Learners Instructional Permit

question: What is the minimum age required to haul hazardous materials?
explanation: The manual states you must be 21 years of age to haul hazardous materials.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Commercial Drivers License Learners Instructional Permit

question: What passing score is required on each CDL knowledge test?
explanation: The manual states a passing score of 80% is required per knowledge test.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Knowledge Tests/Endorsements

question: If you fail a CDL knowledge test for the second time, how long must you wait before retaking that specific test?
explanation: The manual states that if you fail any knowledge test for the second time, you must wait a minimum of seven days before retaking that test.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Knowledge Tests/Endorsements

question: Which knowledge test must be successfully passed before an applicant can proceed to any additional knowledge tests?
explanation: The General Knowledge Test is required for all applicants and must be successfully passed before proceeding to additional knowledge tests.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Knowledge Tests/Endorsements

question: In addition to passing the Hazardous Materials Knowledge Test and providing proof of citizenship or lawful permanent residency, an applicant must also pass what additional federal requirement?
choice_c: A Transportation Security Administration (TSA) background/fingerprint check
explanation: The Administration may not issue a hazardous materials endorsement without TSA approval, which requires an electronic application and fingerprint/background record check.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Knowledge Tests/Endorsements, Hazardous Materials Knowledge Test

question: The CDL Skills Test must be passed in what order?
choice_a: Pre-Trip Inspection, then Basic Control Skills Test, then Public Road Test
choice_b: Any order chosen by the examiner
choice_c: Basic Control Skills Test, then Pre-Trip Inspection, then Public Road Test
choice_d: Public Road Test, then Basic Control Skills, then Pre-Trip Inspection
explanation: The manual states you must pass the Pre-Trip Inspection to continue onto the Basic Control Skills Test, and pass that to continue onto the Public Road Test.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Skills Test Are Administered by Appointment Only

question: On the CDL Basic Control Skills Test, how many total points constitute an automatic failure?
explanation: The manual states a Basic Control Skills Test is based on total points, with 9 points being a failure.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Qualifying Scores

question: On the CDL Public Road Test, how many total points constitute a failure?
explanation: The manual states a Public Road Test is based on total points, with 31 points being a failure.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Qualifying Scores

question: What is the time limit for the Pre-Trip Inspection portion of the CDL skills test?
explanation: The manual lists a Pre-Trip Inspection time limit of 45 minutes for all vehicle classes.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Time Limit (All Vehicle Classes A, B, & C)

question: According to the manual, what time must a CDL test start by on Saturdays?
explanation: The manual states no test will start after 10:00 a.m. on Saturday.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Skills Test Are Administered by Appointment Only

question: A BAC of 0.04% or more while driving a CMV disqualifies a driver for how long on a first offense (non-hazmat vehicle)?
explanation: An alcohol concentration of 0.04% or more while driving a CMV disqualifies the driver from driving a CMV for one year on the first offense.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Driving, Drinking, and Drugs

question: If a driver's CMV was required to be placarded for hazardous materials, a first-offense BAC of 0.04% or more disqualifies the driver for how long?
explanation: The manual states a BAC of 0.04% or more disqualifies a driver for three years if the vehicle was required to be placarded for hazmat, versus one year otherwise.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Driving, Drinking, and Drugs

question: Under Section 1 of the manual, if a driver's BAC test shows any detectable amount of alcohol under 0.04%, what happens?
choice_b: The driver is put out-of-service for 24 hours
choice_d: The driver's CDL is suspended for 30 days
explanation: The manual states that any detectable amount of alcohol under 0.04% puts the driver out-of-service for 24 hours.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.4.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: Refusing to submit to a BAC test in Maryland results in what consequence for a first offense?
choice_a: Disqualification from driving a CMV for one year
explanation: A refusal to submit to a BAC test disqualifies the driver from driving a CMV for one year on the first offense, and for life on a subsequent offense.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Intro, Implied Consent

question: Per the manual, "excessive speeding" as a serious traffic violation means driving how many mph or more above the posted speed limit?
explanation: The manual defines excessive speeding as driving 15 mph or more above the posted speed limit, listed as a serious traffic violation.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.4.3 Serious Traffic Violations

question: A driver who commits two serious traffic violations within a three-year period involving a CMV will lose their CDL for at least how long?
explanation: The manual states you will lose your CDL for at least 60 days for two serious traffic violations within a three-year period.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.4.3 Serious Traffic Violations

question: A first violation of an out-of-service order results in loss of a CDL for at least how long?
explanation: The manual states you will lose your CDL for at least 90 days for a first violation of an out-of-service order.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.4.4 Violation of Out-of-Service Orders

question: A first railroad-highway grade crossing violation results in loss of a CDL for at least how long?
explanation: The manual states you will lose your CDL for at least 60 days for a first railroad-highway grade crossing violation.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.4.5 Railroad-highway Grade Crossing Violations

question: Gross Combination Weight Rating (GCWR) is best defined as:
choice_a: The most a vehicle and trailer can safely weigh together when fully loaded, as set by the manufacturer
choice_b: The weight of the trailer alone when empty
choice_c: The legal maximum weight allowed on any interstate highway
choice_d: The weight of the cargo only, excluding the vehicle
explanation: GCWR is the most a vehicle and trailer can safely weigh together when fully loaded, a limit decided by the vehicle manufacturer.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.1 Commercial Motor Vehicles

question: Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) refers to:
choice_a: The most a single vehicle can safely weigh by itself when fully loaded, including driver, passengers, fuel, and cargo
choice_b: The combined weight of a truck and trailer only
choice_c: The unloaded weight of the vehicle only
choice_d: A weight limit set by the state, not the manufacturer
explanation: GVWR is the most a vehicle can safely weigh by itself when fully loaded, a limit set by the manufacturer, including the vehicle, driver, passengers, fuel, and cargo.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.1 Commercial Motor Vehicles

question: Under "Other CDL Rules," a CDL holder must notify their employer of a traffic conviction (other than parking) within how many days?
explanation: The manual requires notifying your employer within 30 days of conviction of any traffic violation (except parking), no matter what type of vehicle was being driven.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.5 Other CDL Rules

question: Restriction code "E" on a CDL means the driver:
choice_a: Cannot operate a CMV equipped with a manual transmission
choice_b: Cannot operate a CMV equipped with air brakes
choice_d: Cannot operate a passenger vehicle requiring a Class A CDL
explanation: If you pass the skills test in an automatic transmission vehicle, restriction E is applied, showing you are restricted from operating a CMV equipped with a manual transmission.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.2.2 CDL Endorsements & Restrictions, E - No Manual Transmission

question: Restriction code "L" applies to a driver who:
choice_c: Failed or didn't take the air brake portion of the knowledge test, or tested in a vehicle without air brakes
choice_d: Tested in an automatic transmission vehicle
explanation: Restriction L applies when a driver fails or doesn't take the air brake knowledge test component, or takes the skills test in a vehicle without air brakes.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.2.2 CDL Endorsements & Restrictions, L - No Air Brake Equipped CMV

question: Restriction "K" applies to drivers who certify their status as Non-Excepted Intrastate or Excepted Intrastate, restricting them from:
choice_a: Operating a CMV in interstate commerce
explanation: Drivers who certify Non-Excepted Intrastate or Excepted Intrastate status receive a K restriction, showing they are restricted from operating a CMV in interstate commerce.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.2.2 CDL Endorsements & Restrictions, K - Intrastate Only

question: According to Section 1, a CMV driver who does not wear a seatbelt is how many times more likely to be fatally injured if thrown from the vehicle?
explanation: The manual states that if you don't wear a seatbelt, you are four times more likely to be fatally injured if you are thrown from the vehicle.
source_note: Maryland Commercial Driver's License Manual (DL-151, 05/26), Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MDOT MVA) -- Section 1, 1.5 Other CDL Rules
